markdown:
**Region Name.** Velásquez Rainforest Stand

**Population.** ?

**Owner/Leader.** *Unnamed*

**Type.** Settlement

**Founded.** 1282

Sitting a good deal south past [the mountains], during the tail end of the relic wars, a detachment—mostly comprised of Orccs, Gobbos and Humans—began to explore the region in the hopes of cataloguing and mapping them, as well as potentially coming back with any discoveries that would help a Neon City that was still in its infancy. That major detachment eventually found a sealed vault in what was once Durango, a state in the northern part of Mexico.

The vault—named the *Reserva Engramática de Flora y Fauna Mundial "Marta Velásquez"* by the local government at the time—contained a catalog of both worldwide plant and animal life, as well as several old world engrammatic storage devices containing vast swaths of replicable DNA and viable variants of the species that were living on Earth sometime before the Great Collapse. Being that it is a vault located in the middle of the Old World's country of Mexico, it of course has the most complete collection of species native to Mexico itself. Its collection of Eastern European and Russian species is its weakest point—and even those come up to an impressive self-assessment of 79% of all available species at the time of collection.

Over time, the Orccs that headed here from the original detachment settled into the region and began the process of restoration and making reparations with the land itself. Over time, as the rediscovery of technology included them gaining access to terraforming equipment, as well as the tools and tech necessary to engage in wide scale reforestation projects, they spent the next few centuries regrowing the nearby rainforest while also clearing it of the now-endemic Killer Kudzu plagues that readily infested many of the tropical and subtropical regions around the area.

Now, in 1622 and beyond, the Velásquez Rainforest Stand has grown in the place of the *Reserva Engramática*, with a major central pseudo-city settlement that allows for civilized living that proves the Orcc families' tenacity and perseverance in maintaining a healthy relationship with nature around them. An incredibly large amount of once-lost species are regrown and reintroduced here through genetic splicing and cloning projects, and some of the most accomplished biologists to come out of Neon City call the Stand their home.

Orccs make up the majority of the Stand's demographics, with roughly 72% of the population being Orccs. The remaining 28% is majority New Human, with Gobbos being surprisingly more absent here than you'd expect—mostly because of the Gobbos' propensity towards hedonism, versus Orccs' more stoic, noble approach to their cause.

**Creator.** Celica#1988, reny#8234
